“Okay, the fund is 3,000 each,” Sunaina said, writing on the whiteboard in the club room. “Take away the train.”
“That's 1,400,” Jahnavi said.
“Then the dormitory for three nights: 800.”
“So 3,000 minus 2,200 leaves...”
“Eight hundred.”
“For everything else? Food and entry tickets?”
“Only 800. For three days.”
Jahnavi groaned. “I was going to say we could do the fort, the museum and the boat ride.”
“Then we check ticket prices first. Which ones are must-see and which are nice-to-have?”
“Fort and museum. The boat ride is optional.”
“Good. We work with 800, not with what we wish we had.”
Jahnavi copied the two numbers into her notebook and circled the 800.

qa.q: How much is left for food and entry tickets?
qa.a: Only 800 is left for food and entry tickets.

qa.q: What is Jahnavi feeling when she hears that only 800 remains?
qa.a: Jahnavi is disappointed and a little worried, since she groans and then reconsiders her wish list.

qa.q: What could help make the 800 stretch?
qa.a: The group could rank the sights and pay for the must-sees first, then choose cheap local food, since the fixed costs cannot change.

qa.q: How might a classmate who hoped for costly plans see the 800 limit?
qa.a: That classmate may be disappointed at first, but knowing the limit early avoids a nasty surprise and lets everyone choose fairly.

grounding: A group with a fixed trip fund subtracts transport and stay, and sees only a small amount remains for food and tickets.

subtopic: Planning a trip on a budget

passage: Before our Mysore trip last winter, everyone in the group chat was already choosing ice creams. I'm Pranav, and I was the one holding the notebook. Each of us had 3,000 rupees from the school trip kitty. Madhuri said, "Start from the top, not from the fun stuff." So I wrote 3,000 and began taking things away. Bus there and back: 1,150. Two nights in the dormitory: 1,050. I stared at what was left. 800. For two and a half days of meals, the palace ticket, the zoo and any water we'd buy. My stomach dropped a little, honestly. I read it out on our call and the chat went quiet. Then Madhuri said, "Good. Now we know the real number." We cut the zoo and kept the palace. Looking back, that one subtraction saved us from a very hungry last day.

qa.q: How much did the two nights in the dormitory cost each person?
qa.a: The two nights in the dormitory cost 1,050.

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling when the number 800 appeared, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Pranav felt a jolt of worry; the narrator says their stomach dropped a little on seeing how little was left for meals and tickets.

qa.q: What else could the group try if 800 still felt too tight?
qa.a: They could look for a cheaper stay or carry some snacks from home, then redo the subtraction together before booking, so every choice rests on the real number.

qa.q: How might Madhuri see the quiet moment in the chat?
qa.a: Madhuri treats it as useful rather than bad news, because knowing the real number early lets the group decide calmly what to cut.

grounding: Shows teens starting from each person's fixed trip money, subtracting bus and stay first, and finding only 800 left for meals and tickets.

Class 9B trip planning, Thursday. Notes by the class teacher.
The group wanted to begin with the coracle ride at Hampi. I asked them to start from the other end instead. Parveen wrote 3,000 at the top of the board, the amount each student has. Vishal read out the train fare, 1,300 return, and Parveen took it away. Then the guesthouse, 900 for two nights. "So... 800 for everything else?" Vishal said, and laughed nervously. Parveen kept going, half under her breath: "Three days, six meals at least, the site tickets. The coracle is 300. That's too big a piece of 800." Nobody argued. They crossed out the ride and wrote "maybe, if money is left" beside it.
Next step: on Monday I will bring the guesthouse's menu prices so they can test the food part of the plan.

qa.q: What was the return train fare?
How can you tell that Parveen was worried about the coracle ride?
qa.a: Parveen sounded concerned, listing the meals and site tickets still to be paid and saying 300 was too big a piece of the 800.

qa.q: What would you change first if the guesthouse menu turns out costly?
qa.a: The group could plan some meals at cheaper local stalls, then redo the subtraction with the new food cost before adding back any extra ride.

qa.q: How might Vishal see the plan once the ride was crossed out?
qa.a: Vishal may be a little let down about the ride but also relieved to know the real limit, since Vishal's nervous laugh showed the 800 was a surprise.

grounding: Illustrates a group working backward from each student's fixed trip amount, taking away train fare and stay to see that only 800 remains for food and tickets.
